version.changelog: Quality fixes: removed third-party references, aligned docs with implementation

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: sql-generator
Version: 2.3.0

The SQL Generator skill bundle is a legitimate utility designed to generate SQL templates for table creation, queries, indexing, and mock data. The core logic in `scripts/sql.sh` uses standard bash commands to process user input and output formatted SQL strings to stdout without executing them or making network calls. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection was found; the script's behavior aligns perfectly with its stated purpose.

llm.summary: The skill appears to be a local SQL template/generator and mostly coherent with its description, but there are small mismatches between the human instructions and the shipped script and the provided script was truncated so I cannot fully verify there is no unexpected behavior.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (SQL generation, explain, optimize, DDL, mock data, migrations) aligns with the included script which generates CREATE TABLE/DDL and other SQL artifacts. Minor inconsistency: SKILL.md lists command names (query, explain, optimize, create, mock, migrate, cheatsheet) while scripts/sql.sh supports commands named table, query, join, index, migrate, seed, explain, convert — this mismatch could cause confusion or lead an agent to pass unexpected arguments.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is an instruction-only manifest and does not tell the agent to read system files, environment variables, or contact external endpoints. The shipped script (sql.sh) is a local generator that formats SQL and prints to stdout; the visible portions do not perform network calls, file exfiltration, or credential access. However the script content in the package was truncated in the review artifact (shown as '…[truncated]'), so I cannot confirm the remainder contains no I/O, exec, or network behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — code is packaged as script files only. There is no remote download/install step in the metadata, which reduces supply-chain risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, no primary credential, and no config paths. The visible script does not reference environment secrets. This is proportionate for a local SQL generation tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill doesn't request persistent system-wide privileges or modify other skills' configurations. Agent-autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not in itself a red flag here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This appears to be a local SQL template/generator and mostly matches its description, but note two things before installing: (1) SKILL.md and the bundled script use different command names — confirm which commands your agent will invoke to avoid surprises; (2) the provided script content was truncated in the review data, so verify the full scripts/sql.sh contents yourself (search for network calls, calls to curl/wget/git, child_process/exec usage, reads of ~/.aws or other config files, or eval/execution of untrusted text). Run the skill in a sandbox or limited-permission environment first, and avoid giving it any credentials or access to sensitive databases until you inspect the full code.
